still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and the oral Wegovy starting dose still costs $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

The April 2033 Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India is still in force, India's export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer shipments still apply, and Beijing's WTO complaint is still unresolved.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 43.0% ever-used minus 32.4% current leaves 10.6% of adults who used and are off now. About 50% of current users are on a second or later course (16.2 points), and 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (16.2 + 3.0) / 43.0 ≈ 44.7% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.6 points stopped once and have not restarted. One-year persistence is still about one-third on self-managed weekly and oral products, ~65% on monthly MariTide, and ~60% inside conditioned Medicare, Medicaid and employer tracks. Restart within a year is 36–47%. Medicare's 12-month lockout after a failed six-month progress check produces a new kind of forced stop. Ever-use rose 8.4 points, inside the 10.8 limit, mostly from 65+ adults entering the Jan 2036 Medicare benefit and young smokers and vapers entering through the Feb 2036 nicotine label. Age check (adult weights 0.20/0.33/0.24/0.23): 4.0 + 10.23 + 9.48 + 8.67 ≈ 32.4. The income thirds average 32.4. Users: 32.4% of ~277M adults ≈ 89.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare 26.5M (29.5%, of which ~24.0M are 65+ and ~10.0M are on the new weight-only benefit); Medicaid 12.0M (13.4%: ~5.4M on weight use in the 19 enhanced-match states, ~1.5M AUD, ~1.6M nicotine, and the rest on diabetes and other codes); commercial 20.5M (22.9%, ~11.8M in conditioned tracks); legitimate cash 25.5M (28.4%, including ~3.6M calm/focus subscribers and ~5.0M on the indefinite $149 starting dose); imported or counterfeit 5.2M (5.8%). Sum: 26.5 + 12.0 + 20.5 + 25.5 + 5.2 = 89.7. Public programmes pay for 38.5M users (43%), and Medicare is now the largest single payer. 65+ check: 24.0M / ~63.7M ≈ 37.7%. Adult obesity ~30.9%. About 15% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the 31 states without enhanced Medicaid coverage (most of the rural South among them), among uninsured adults aged 26–64, and among people who refuse on principle. That last group is newly visible as the 'Undosed'. On-label nicotine users ≈ 3.2M across payers (Medicaid 1.6, cash 0.7, commercial 0.6, Medicare 0.3). Pediatric: 2.0% of under-18s, ~3.8% of 12–17s and ~0.6% of 6–11s; ~62% of 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP under EPSDT. About 6.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, ~0.9M of them because of a Medicare or Medicaid lockout.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare (~26.5M users). Since Jan 2036 the Medicare Obesity Treatment and Accountability Act (signed Sep 2035) covers incretins for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity, through Part D at a uniform negotiated net price of ~$185/month and a $50 copay. Coverage requires verified adherence (a monthly clinic dose, PBM fills plus a connected-cap log, or a smart-bottle log), ≥5% weight loss at six months and a baseline DXA for anyone 65+. Failing the six-month check triggers a 12-month lockout. A documented 'bone holiday' (T-score decline ≥0.5 or a fragility fracture) pauses the clock without a lockout. Spend arithmetic at the Dec 2036 run rate: weight benefit 10.0M × $185 × 12 ≈ $22.2B; legacy routes (diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk, AUD, nicotine) 16.5M × ~$212 × 12 ≈ $42.0B; total ≈ $64.2B a year, up from $38.3B. Calendar-2036 spend is lower (~$53B) because the benefit ramped through the year. CBO's ten-year score for the weight benefit: ~9M average users × $175 × 12 ≈ $18.9B/yr, × 10 ≈ $189B gross, less ~$26B in beneficiary premium share and ~$15B in assumed offsets, ≈ $148B net federal over 2036–2045. Medicaid (~12.0M). The Act offers 80% federal match through FY2039 to states that cover adult weight use under the same continuation criteria, and 19 states took it, up from 7. Tobacco-cessation drugs cannot be excluded from Medicaid (ACA §2502), so the Foundayo nicotine label became a covered outpatient drug in every state in Feb 2036, as AUD did in 2033. Arithmetic: 12.0M × ~$160 net × 12 ≈ $23.0B, of which ~$16B is federal. Children 6–11 still reach semaglutide through EPSDT.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–28 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $18–55 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses under the unchanged tariff and export-licence regime, the price is ~$85–170. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China still supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume and send more of it to the Gulf, Nigeria and Mexico.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline through negotiated channels; list prices did not move. TrumpRx: the Wegovy pill starting dose is unchanged at $149 and maintenance fell from $199 to $179. Foundayo is $149–199. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound fell from $249–299 to $219–249. Oral amycretin got a TrumpRx price of $279 in Jul 2035, down from ~$449 cash direct. MariTide is $229 direct, and the at-home autoinjector carries the same price. Retatrutide is ~$299 cash. Medicare's uniform weight-benefit net price is ~$185. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 36% of employers cover weight use and ~72% of those impose conditions. ~11.8M people are in commercial tracks. Many employers now waive the ACA-permitted tobacco surcharge (up to 50% of premium) for enrolees on a logged Foundayo quit course. Route mix: orals ~49% of users, weekly injectables ~39%, monthly MariTide ~11% (~9.5M, up from 5.8M). Gray market: 5.2M users, down from 5.8M. Branded prices came down toward gray delivered prices, but counterfeits and domestic re-fills persist among the uninsured in non-expansion states.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)

GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide), clinic-administered and, since Nov 2035, an at-home monthly autoinjector with a connected dose cap
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo), including the smoking/vaping cessation label since Feb 2036
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults (orforglipron / Foundayo, approved Feb 2036)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth-velocity, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening language
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide). The 60+ without-CVD extension received a Complete Response Letter in Mar 2036
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans via telehealth (~3.6M subscribers), now screened with both AUDIT-C and the Fagerström nicotine test, so that ~45% are written on the AUD or nicotine label
sub-threshold 'drink less' and 'vape less' use by people who do not meet disorder criteria, especially 18–29s
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid, which continues after the CRL
semaglutide at above-label titration in 12–14-year-olds in gray channels
bimagrumab bought cash or gray by upper-income users who are not at high fracture risk, as 'muscle insurance'
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Lilly filed orforglipron for smoking and vaping cessation in Jan 2035 on a phase 3 that matched varenicline's 24-week continuous abstinence (~33% vs ~31%) with ~4 kg less post-quit weight gain. Approval came Feb 2036, 13 months after filing. The monthly/implant driver is realised with existing products in a new form, as the approval rules require. Amgen's MariTide at-home monthly autoinjector with a connected dose cap was approved Nov 2035 as a device-and-formulation supplement. It plus the Medicare benefit's acceptance of monthly clinic or connected doses as 'verified adherence' moved ~9.5M people onto monthly dosing. Subdermal implants (6- and 12-month) remain in phase 2 and are not on the US market. One 6-month implant entered phase 3 in 2036. Lilly resubmitted tirzepatide for dementia risk in adults 60+ without CVD in Mar 2035, and FDA issued a CRL in Mar 2036 asking for fracture-mitigation data in women 70+. Bimagrumab's sNDA for adults 65+ on incretins with sarcopenia (filed Jun 2035) is under review with an early-2037 goal date. ~0.4M are on the existing high-fracture-risk label, a group that has widened as more users meet it. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. US branded net prices fell ~6–8% a year through negotiated channels. The global incretin market is ~$225B (2035).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. Older Medicare starters report more dehydration-related ED visits during titration. Monthly MariTide front-loads nausea in the first days after each dose.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. The Medicare benefit pays for one titration-support pharmacist visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first MDL gastroparesis bellwether (Mar 2035) ended in a defence verdict on general causation. A second settled confidentially. GI claims held at ~41,000, and recruitment shifted toward Medicare starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. Persistence after stopping is still disputed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Cholecystectomy volume in 65+ rose with Medicare uptake.
No causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; still pleaded together with EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now recognised as a population problem. The NEJM Medicare-claims analysis (Apr 2035) found the age-adjusted 65+ hip-fracture rate rose ~5% from 2031 to 2034, the first sustained rise in two decades. It attributes ~14,000 excess hip fractures a year to more than 2 years of incretin use (HR ~1.3, ~1.45 after three or more cycles, worse in women 70+ and with EPI). DXA studies show ~25–40% of weight lost is lean mass in 65+ users without resistance training.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling (Jul 2035) expanded Warnings: baseline DXA for users 65+ and those with fracture risk factors, protein and resistance-training counselling, and fracture risk weighed at each cycle. The Medicare Act wrote baseline DXA and a 'bone holiday' exemption into coverage. USPSTF began an update of osteoporosis screening that names incretin use as a risk factor. Bimagrumab sNDA under review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the first year of nicotine-label users. The pediatric psychiatric signal concerns restrictive eating.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2033 FDA observational figures stand: ~7% at maintenance doses vs ~3.5% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. A low-dose substudy began in 2035 with no readout. Calm subscribers grew to ~3.6M. Several platforms now sell low-dose plans to smokers as 'quiet the urge'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. Three untitled letters to calm platforms; no enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Medicare and Medicaid lockouts after failed six-month checks created ~1.1M forced stops in 2036. Bone holidays add planned stops whose regain is not yet characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Act's lockout is under CMS review after the first-year data. No change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency; thiamine in AUD users who keep drinking; low ferritin in adolescent girls. Protein insufficiency is common in 65+ users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; thiamine counselling on the AUD label; protein counselling added in Jul 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims reached ~57,000. Novo is negotiating a global settlement inside its $6.2B reserve. The DOJ civil investigative demand is ongoing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI wording on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels. FDA closed out the Form 483 after Novo's corrective plan in 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are poorly characterised, and so are lockout-driven and bone-holiday stops. There are no data on indefinite starting-dose use, and none on decade-long monthly antibody-conjugate exposure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density and growth PMRs continue. CMS funds a Medicare long-term outcomes registry built on verified-adherence feeds.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~36,000. A second re-filled-vial cluster (2035, Alabama and Georgia, ~90 infections, 1 death) followed the 2034 Burkholderia cluster. Re-filling concentrates in non-expansion states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tariff and export checks unchanged. No statute changed. Two state attorneys general prosecuted re-fill operators under existing pharmacy law.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Height velocity still ~0.5–0.6 cm/year below expected in prepubertal starters, with partial catch-up after stopping. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. The bone wave brought new scrutiny of adolescent bone-mineral accrual, and an interim PMR shows lower lumbar BMD Z-scores in 12–17 long-term users. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language unchanged and no REMS. AAP added a DXA consideration for adolescents on more than 2 years of treatment. AAP still prefers lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Still ~1 per 2,000 person-years in ED-network data, concentrated in titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling; the postmarketing study is ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Nicotine-label harms (combined GI and withdrawal symptoms, dual use with NRT, relapse-weight rebound)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Early pharmacy data show more first-month nausea discontinuation in heavy vapers aged 18–25. Little is known about what happens to weight when the course ends and the person stays quit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling; a postmarketing study of 12-month relapse and weight is required.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volume is down ~15–16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. The Medicare wave shifted the senior basket. Oral nutrition shakes, high-protein yoghurt and 'soft protein' meals for 65+ users grow double digits, and Abbott and Nestlé Health Science market directly to the DXA-scanned. In the 19 enhanced-match states the 2033 'tariff bounce' in low-income snack volume has reversed. In non-expansion states, from Mississippi to Texas, it has not.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. Tobacco is now the faster-falling vice. In the first ten months after the Foundayo label, cigarette shipments fell ~9% and closed-system vape sales ~12% year on year. Altria and Reynolds announced ~2,100 job cuts across Richmond and Winston-Salem. Bardstown distilleries keep laydown low. Non-alcoholic and 'calm' drinks are ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Senior-heavy chains (Cracker Barrel, Bob Evans, Golden Corral) rebuilt menus around protein-forward small plates after the Medicare benefit took effect. Bar revenue keeps falling in Midwestern mid-sized cities. 'Undosed' supper clubs and bakeries in Asheville and Boise are a small but much-photographed niche.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, now in women's 60+ lines too. Adaptive and compression wear for older users grows, and so does hip-protector underwear, a category that barely existed. Resale serves cyclers. In non-expansion states, size-up returns from regainers keep rising.

fitness.state: Strength training is now prescribed. FDA counselling language plus Medicare Advantage gym benefits made SilverSneakers-style resistance classes the fastest-growing senior offering, and physical-therapy clinics run 'GLP-1 strength' blocks billed as fall prevention. Track contracts still require InBody scans.

insurance.state: The Part D base beneficiary premium rose again for 2036 and is projected to rise for 2037 as the weight benefit ramps. Part D plans run the verification, lockout and DXA rules, which grows the vendor layer. Employer coverage reached 36% with ~72% conditioned, and tobacco-surcharge waivers are tied to logged quit courses. State Medicaid budgets in the 19 enhanced-match states face a 2039 cliff when federal match falls to the regular rate.

pharma.state: Volume is up and price down. Medicare made itself the largest single buyer at ~$185 net. Lilly gained the nicotine label and kept tirzepatide's dementia ambitions alive despite the CRL. Amgen's monthly MariTide is the Medicare favourite because a monthly dose is easy to verify. Novo stabilised after the 483 close-out, kept oral amycretin growing and is settling EPI inside its reserve. Bone-density diagnostics (Hologic DXA) and osteoporosis drugs grew with the fracture wave.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now also signals your age and your Medicare paperwork. A 70-year-old who is thinner, slower on stairs and carries a DXA printout in her purse is on the benefit. A monthly clinic bruise, or a connected cap clicking on the kitchen counter, means verified. A grandmother who suddenly regained in March missed her six-month 5% and is locked out until next year. In the young, a vaper who stopped vaping and did not gain weight reads as a Foundayo quit. A soft, broad, deliberately unscanned body now reads, for the first time, as a choice: 'Undosed'.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is still the class uniform, and bone is the new status measure in the upper tier: T-scores get mentioned at dinner in Bethesda. Medicare flattened the old-age gradient. Low-income seniors in Cleveland and Tulsa now get the same drug as retirees in Naples, though the Naples retirees also buy bimagrumab and a trainer. The sharpest divide is now by state. In the 19 enhanced-match states poor adults are covered, while in Mississippi and Texas uninsured working-age adults are the most visibly un-medicated group, and they did not choose it.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals stay short. Senior centres in Ohio rebuilt congregate meals around protein targets. The Undosed made bread, butter and long tables their emblem, and Bread Alone (~1,300 congregations) now co-hosts 'Undosed Sundays' with MAHA homeschool networks in Tennessee and Idaho. School fights moved from recording 6–11 medications to whether PE teachers should run resistance training for medicated adolescents.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps now offer 'Undosed' as a profile badge, and it is the fastest-growing tag among 25–40s in Boise, Asheville and Chattanooga. Undosed users often filter out medicated matches. Medicated users joke that the badge means 'will judge your fridge'. The 'quitting on Foundayo' tag appears alongside 'on AUD treatment'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite, thirst, craving and now the urge to smoke are noise a subscription manages. For the Undosed, appetite is evidence of being unmanaged and is defended as such. Their aesthetic is linen, cast iron, visible softness, hand-milled flour and phones left at the door, and their slogan, 'Hungry and Free', is printed on tote bags sold in Whole Foods. The movement splits two ways. Its MAHA wing calls the drugs a federal dependency programme. Its progressive fat-liberation wing calls the Medicare lockout eugenic. Both oppose the conditions, for opposite reasons.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The only measured rates are still the FDA's ~7% vs ~3.5% at maintenance doses and ~10% on retatrutide. Calm/focus subscribers grew from 2.4M to ~3.6M, all inside the 25.5M cash users. Platforms now screen with AUDIT-C and Fagerström, and ~45% of subscribers carry an AUD or nicotine diagnosis that makes 'craving-free' an on-label claim. The FDA low-dose substudy has not read out, so blunting at calm-plan doses is still unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Platforms sell a feature: 'quiet the noise', 'quiet the bottle' and now 'quiet the urge'. Lilly says 'quit without the weight'. CMS says 'verified adherence'. Geriatricians call blunting 'apathy' and check whether it is depression or the drug. The Undosed call it 'the managed life'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 11.8M employees are in conditioned commercial tracks. Waiving the tobacco surcharge for logged Foundayo courses gives quitting a premium-tier logic too. Warehouse and call-centre employers in Columbus and Memphis bundle AUD and nicotine pills into EAPs. FMCSA's guidance still covers on-label AUD use and now nicotine use, and is still silent on calm plans. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved, and a third, from an Undosed employee in Nashville denied the wellness tier for refusing the drug, was filed in 2036.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir now has a sub-shelf, the lockout memoir. Undosed folk and bluegrass nights in Asheville are an indie-press darling, sold explicitly as 'music you can feel'. Netflix's 'dry' stand-up genre has a senior strand about the monthly clinic. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs. Smoke breaks, the last workday ritual of idle talk, are disappearing at Southern plants.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The monthly dose date replaced the weekly shot day for ~9.5M people, and for Medicare couples it is a shared outing. Couples therapists report the pill-sober mismatch, and now the quitter-smoker mismatch. In older couples a new conflict: one spouse is locked out and regaining while the other stays verified.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Medicare Act passed with bipartisan votes as a frailty and dementia measure sold to AARP and fiscal hawks together. The conditions were the price of the CBO score. In 2036 primaries Undosed-aligned candidates won two Idaho legislative seats and a Tennessee state senate primary on 'no conditions on our bodies', yet no state passed a ban on conditioning. Seniors locked out after failed six-month checks are now an organised complaint, and the AARP has asked CMS to soften the 12-month rule. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, permissive on approvals, and now administrative at scale. FDA approved the nicotine label and the MariTide autoinjector, added class bone and muscle warnings, issued a CRL on the dementia extension and sent untitled letters to calm platforms. CMS runs the largest adherence-verification system in the country. No state legislature passed a ban on conditioning. Illinois's remains the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Medicare Obesity Treatment and Accountability Act (signed Sep 2035, effective Jan 2036) is the first federal weight-loss drug benefit. It comes with a negotiated ~$185 net price, a $50 copay, verified adherence, ≥5% loss at six months, a 12-month lockout, baseline DXA for 65+ and a bone-holiday exemption. 19 states took the 80% federal match for adult weight coverage under the same criteria. Nicotine-label coverage became mandatory in Medicaid under ACA §2502 without new statute. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Now federal and default. Part D sponsors receive adherence feeds from clinic MariTide doses, PBM fills, connected caps and smart bottles, plus six-month weights uploaded by clinicians or by cellular scales issued under the benefit. FEHB, employer tracks and 21 state Medicaid programmes (the 19 expansion states plus the two prior conditioners) apply parallel rules. CMS's AUD coding audit now covers nicotine diagnoses from calm platforms too. Benefit brokers still buy de-identified 'focus' cohorts.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD and nicotine labels under existing rules. DoD tobacco-cessation programmes added Foundayo, and the Army recruit oral weight pilot continues without expansion. The VA adopted the Medicare continuation criteria for its weight programme. FMCSA guidance now covers on-label nicotine use.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 2033 Section 232 tariff and India's export-licence checks stand. Beijing's WTO case is still before a panel. Lower branded US prices narrowed the gap with gray imports, and Indian exporters sell more to the Gulf, Nigeria and Mexico. Smuggled API still feeds domestic re-filling, mainly in non-expansion Southern states. Amgen expanded US fill-finish in Ohio for MariTide, and Lilly added US oral capacity in North Carolina.

events.event: An NEJM analysis of Medicare claims finds the age-adjusted hip-fracture rate in Americans 65+ rose for the first time in two decades and attributes about 14,000 excess hip fractures a year to long-term incretin use; in July FDA adds class-wide bone and muscle warnings with baseline DXA for users 65+

President signs the Medicare Obesity Treatment and Accountability Act: from January 2036 Part D covers weight-loss incretins at a negotiated ~$185 net and a $50 copay, but only with verified adherence, 5% loss at six months, baseline bone scans for seniors and a 12-month lockout for those who fail; 19 states take an 80% federal match to cover Medicaid adults under the same rules
events.driver: coverage_shift: public_expansion; state_action: benefits_conditioning; price_path: managed_decline

events.event: FDA approves an at-home monthly autoinjector for Amgen's MariTide with a connected dose cap; CMS lists monthly clinic or connected doses as verified adherence under the new benefit, and monthly users climb to about 9.5 million by end-2036
events.driver: next_gen_launch: monthly_or_implant (existing product in new form; implants remain in phase 2)

events.event: FDA approves Lilly's Foundayo pill for smoking and vaping cessation, filed in January 2035, after a trial showing varenicline-level quit rates with less weight gain; because federal law bars Medicaid from excluding tobacco-cessation drugs, every state must cover it, and 3.2 million people are on the label by December

FDA issues a Complete Response Letter on tirzepatide for dementia-risk reduction in adults 60+ without heart disease, citing hip fractures in women over 70; calm platforms the same month begin selling low-dose 'quiet the urge' plans to smokers written on the new label

Dating apps add an 'Undosed' badge after a summer of Undosed supper clubs in Asheville and Boise; Undosed-aligned candidates win two Idaho legislative primaries and a Tennessee state senate primary on opposition to drug conditions in benefits, though no state passes a ban

open_tensions: Medicare made itself the default payer just as the bone signal became a population problem. The benefit's 12-month lockout and bone holidays force stops in the oldest, frailest users. Nobody knows whether regain after a forced or bone-motivated stop is safer for a 74-year-old's hip than staying on.

The verification apparatus built for Medicare now covers ~38 million public and ~12 million commercial users. The data that decides who keeps coverage is also the only long-term safety registry. The Undosed, the AARP and the fat-liberation left all attack it, and for incompatible reasons.

The nicotine label put a third craving on-label for calm platforms, with ~45% of 3.6M subscribers now carrying an addiction diagnosis that makes 'craving-free' a legal claim. Low-dose blunting is still unmeasured, and CMS's coding audit now spans two labels.

Enhanced federal Medicaid match ends in FY2039, and 31 states never took it. The class divide on the drug has become a map. Uninsured working-age adults in the South remain the main market for re-filled vials, and the people least able to choose are being counted among the 'unmedicated'.

prose.headline: Medicare Pays, Medicare Watches: A Third of America Is On It, the Hips Are Breaking, and the 'Undosed' Want Out
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, nearly ninety million people, and the biggest single payer is now the federal government. For a decade Medicare covered these drugs for almost everything except weight. Since January it covers weight too. The Medicare Obesity Treatment and Accountability Act passed in September 2035 with votes from both parties, sold as a frailty and dementia bill. Its price was the price that made the budget score possible: about $185 a month to the manufacturers, $50 to the patient, and a set of conditions. You must prove you take the drug, through a clinic dose, a pharmacy fill, a cap that logs each injection or a bottle that logs each pill. You must lose five percent in six months. If you are over sixty-five you must have a bone scan first. If you miss the six-month target you are out for a year.

The bone scan is there because of the hips. In April 2035 researchers reading Medicare claims found that hip fractures among older Americans had begun to rise for the first time in twenty years, about fourteen thousand extra a year among long-term users. They were mostly women over seventy, mostly people who had lost muscle along with fat. The FDA added warnings that summer. Senior centres in Dayton now run resistance classes, and diners in Ohio sell protein plates. A new kind of underwear, padded at the hip, sells in pharmacies. The same fractures cost Lilly its bid to sell tirzepatide for dementia prevention to healthy sixty-year-olds. The FDA wants to know who will break before it says yes.

Most people on the drug no longer think about it weekly. Amgen's MariTide is injected once a month, either in a clinic or by a pen with a connected cap, and Medicare treats either as proof. Nine and a half million people now live on a monthly calendar, and for older couples the clinic visit is something they do together. Implants are still in trials.

In February the drug acquired a third craving. Lilly's pill Foundayo was approved to help people quit smoking and vaping, matching the old quit-smoking pills but without the weight gain. Federal law bars Medicaid from refusing quit-smoking drugs, so every state must cover it, as every state had to cover the alcohol label in 2033. Cigarette shipments fell, and the tobacco companies cut jobs in Richmond and Winston-Salem. The telehealth calm platforms, which already sold low doses as freedom from food noise and drink, now advertise 'quiet the urge' to smokers. Nearly half their customers carry an addiction diagnosis that makes the claim legal.

Prices fell, but not by much. The starting pill is still $149, most brands sell between $179 and $299, and the list price on the box is still $1,349. Nineteen states took federal money to cover poor adults. Thirty-one did not. In Mississippi and much of Texas, uninsured working adults still buy refilled vials from people who mix smuggled powder in back rooms, and the vials are still occasionally lethal.

Against all of this a movement has grown that calls itself Undosed. Its members bake, eat at long tables, refuse the scans and wear their softness on purpose. Dating apps added the badge in June. In Idaho and Tennessee Undosed candidates won primaries arguing that no one's benefits should depend on a log. They passed nothing. The movement's religious wing calls the drugs dependency. Its left wing calls the lockout cruelty. Their complaints about the system point in opposite directions.

The country drinks less, smokes less and weighs less than it did. Everyone in the system is counted, everyone outside it is watched, and the first regains in the Medicare population are showing on the bathroom scales of people over seventy.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dolores Pruitt, sixty-nine, drove a school bus in Dayton for thirty-one years. On the first Tuesday of the month she puts on the good cardigan.

Walt drives. He is on it too, but his clinic is Thursdays, so on Tuesdays he waits in the Kroger lot doing the crossword. At the clinic the nurse scans Dolores's Medicare card, then her arm. One pinch. The screen says VERIFIED in green and she always feels she has passed something.

"Nine point one percent," the nurse says. "You're fine through June." Then, kindly: "DXA in August. Keep doing your bands."

The bands are purple and live on the doorknob. Dolores does her twelve squats holding the counter while the kettle boils. Her sister Ruth missed the six-month mark by four pounds in March and is locked out until next spring. Ruth calls it 'the penalty box' and has started baking again.

At lunch Dolores manages half a turkey sandwich and a protein shake the colour of a peach. The copay is fifty dollars. The cap on Walt's leftover pen box blinks blue on the windowsill, like a smoke detector.

In the afternoon her grandson Tyler, twenty-two, drops by on his way to the warehouse. He shows her the Medicaid card on his phone and the Foundayo bottle in his pocket. Three weeks without the vape. "I don't even want it," he says, puzzled, as if he'd lost his keys.

At the bakery on Brown Street the girl at the register wears an UNDOSED pin. Dolores buys a loaf for Ruth and holds it in both hands, warm, all the way to the car.

least_plausible_claims.quote: A grandmother who suddenly regained in March missed her six-month 5% and is locked out until next year.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the weight-only Medicare benefit and its six-month check begin in Jan 2036, so no one can fail that check by March. The same impossible timeline appears in the prose, where Ruth 'missed the six-month mark by four pounds in March'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In the first ten months after the Foundayo label, cigarette shipments fell ~9% and closed-system vape sales ~12% year on year.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: about 3.2M label users, roughly 1M of them successful quitters, against a base of tens of millions of smokers and vapers, would not plausibly produce a 9% cigarette drop in ten months. The causal attribution is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare 26.5M (29.5%, of which ~24.0M are 65+ and ~10.0M are on the new weight-only benefit)
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 10M new weight-only enrollees in the first calendar year would each need a baseline DXA (for the 65+ share), verified-adherence setup and a prior-authorisation pass. The capacity and ramp are not shown, and the 65+ rate jumps from 21.5% to 37.7% in two years.

rationale.badness: Measured against the 2026 reference, the candidate keeps its 2034 harms and adds a federal adherence-verification system, 12-month lockouts producing ~1.1M forced stops, and a ~14,000-per-year hip-fracture excess. It also keeps pediatric growth deceleration, re-filled-vial infections and deaths, and an unmeasured low-dose blunting rate under a 3.6M-subscriber calm market. Access broadens, obesity and smoking fall, and poor seniors are covered, which offsets some harm. Autonomy is the worst dimension (default conditioning, premium tiers, and lockouts that fall on the frail). Inequality has shifted from income to a state-by-state map (19 vs 31 states) rather than shrinking.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: +7.8 pp adoption, managed decline (6–8% a year), the Medicare Act, a nicotine label filed Jan 2035 and approved Feb 2036, the hip-fracture wave, the MariTide autoinjector as an allowed 'new form', benefits conditioning, the Undosed movement and the marketed-feature personality layer. mechanism: the chains are mostly shown (the NEJM study leads to FDA warnings and Medicare's DXA and bone-holiday rules; ACA §2502 leads to Medicaid nicotine coverage). But the March six-month-failure timeline is impossible for a Jan 2036 benefit (claim 1), the cigarette-decline attribution is asserted (claim 2), and the Undosed rise is thinly caused. magnitude: on-drug 32.4%, ever-used 43%, income thirds, age bands, cycling (44.7%), payer mix (sum 89.7M), Medicare spend ($64.2B), CBO ($148B net) and Medicaid ($23B) all reconcile and sit inside the envelope. The weaknesses are the aggressive first-year uptake of 10M weight-only enrollees (claim 3) and the large tobacco effect.
rationale.generativity: The day-in-the-life scene is concrete: Dolores's VERIFIED screen, the purple bands on the doorknob, Ruth in 'the penalty box', Tyler's Foundayo bottle and the Undosed bakery pin. The world fields imply many more scenes: lockout memoirs, DXA printouts, senior-centre resistance classes, Undosed supper clubs, EEOC charges and primary campaigns. The one flaw is a prose timeline that clashes with the benefit's start date.
